newsitem.title: USA: Sprint sees 1997 EPS off, remains bullish.
newsitem.headline: Sprint sees 1997 EPS off, remains bullish.

text.p: Sprint Corp said Tuesday it expects earnings per share to decline for 1997 compared with 1996 due to increased investment, but the telecommunications company said it is bullish about its prospects.

"We expect our earnings per share will decline in 1997 compared with 1996 levels, primarily due to the increased early stage losses associated with Sprint Spectrum and our expansion into the competitive markets," Arthur Krause, chief financial officer, told analysts on a teleconference. "Irrespective of this near-term earnings trend, we are very bullish about our prospects," he said.

Kansas City-based Sprint said its long-distance business continues to post strong results. The company reported fourth quarter long distance revenues rose 12.3 percent to $2.16 billion, and minutes of use were up 21 percent from fourth quarter 1995.
"We currently see no impediments to this momentum and we are targetting double-digit volume and revenue growth for the full year of 1997," Krause said.
"We currently expect long distance to generate double-digit operating income growth in the first quarter and for all of 1997," he said.

Krause said, however, first quarter volume growth may trend downward slightly due in part to the lack of toll-free lines for the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, which in the past had a strong seasonal impact.
"This traffic has traditionally had a lower average yield, so the reported gap between minutes and revenues should narrow," Krause said.

Krause said he also expects Sprint's local telephone segment to post double-digit earnings growth in the first quarter, as demand for secondary telephone lines and "class services" such as call waiting and caller I.D. is growing.
Local telephone operating income rose 12.4 percent in the fourth quarter to $334 million, the company said, and the number of access lines grew 5.6 percent to more than 7.1 million.
"We currently expect that our local operations will also achieve double-digit profit growth in the first quarter and we are targeting similar growth for all of 1997," Krause said.

Krause said under the Telecommunications Act the company hopes to provide local service in two to three dozen cities by the year-end, but "this may be an aggressive target" because of interconnection issues.
Krause pointed out that the company's investments in Sprint PCS, for example, will continue to pressure earnings in the near term.
"As Sprint Spectrum (PCS) rolls out additional markets and gains subscribers, related earnings dilution will increase," he said.

Sprint said its fourth quarter results include $65 million in after-tax losses or $0.15 a share, related to Global One and the buildout of Sprint PCS. Global One is a joint venture of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint.
Sprint said the buildout of the platform for its consumer Internet access business, however, is substantially complete.
"We expect this service will exit 1997 with an annualized revenue stream in the neighborhood of $100 million," Krause said.

Earlier, Sprint reported fourth quarter net income of $0.57 a share versus a loss of $0.98. Fourth quarter income from continuing operations before ventures and non-recurring charges was $347 million compared with $290 million.
